answers.label: Integration purpose
answers.answer: Mellox AI lets authenticated business and agency workspace editors edit selected marketing images and carousels in Canva, then import edited PNG pages into their own Mellox workspace. Access is workspace-scoped. Users initiate design creation and import; Mellox does not enumerate their entire Canva library.

answers.label: OAuth state and authorization
answers.answer: We use server-side authorization-code OAuth with S256 PKCE. State and verifier each use 48 random bytes. The database stores hashed state and an encrypted verifier, bound to the authenticated user and workspace. State expires after ten minutes and is consumed once. Final credential installation rechecks membership and state in a transaction; withdrawal prevents a pending callback from installing credentials.

answers.label: Redirect URL restrictions
answers.answer: The callback is fixed by server configuration: https://mellox.ai/api/integrations/canva/callback. Production requires a non-loopback HTTPS origin. Credentials, query strings, fragments and non-root paths are rejected in APP_URL. Clients cannot choose the OAuth callback. Post-connect return paths must be internal relative paths. The exact callback must also be registered in Canva Developer Portal.

answers.label: Scopes and least privilege
answers.answer: Requested scopes: asset:write uploads selected images; asset:read checks upload jobs; design:content:write creates/imports designs; design:meta:read retrieves design editor links; design:content:read exports PNG pages. All five support implemented actions. We do not request profile, folder, brand-template, collaboration or webhook scopes.

answers.label: Token encryption and storage
answers.answer: Access and refresh tokens are encrypted with AES-256-GCM and fresh 12-byte IVs, in separate columns of the same service-role-only Supabase Postgres record. Keys remain in server environment configuration; the default key is provider-specific HKDF-SHA256 derived from the Supabase service credential. A compatible dedicated key supports older grants. Tokens are not returned to browsers. We do not claim KMS/HSM or independent physical token stores.

answers.label: Access controls
answers.answer: Requests require Supabase authentication and server-side workspace role checks. Canva mutations require editor or higher; viewers can read connection status. Credential tables deny anonymous and authenticated database roles; credential functions are executable only by service_role. Mapping tables enforce workspace RLS. Actual staff access, MFA and production administrative privileges require operator confirmation.

answers.label: Webhook signature verification
answers.answer: Not applicable to this implementation: no Canva webhook receiver, webhook subscription code or collaboration event scope is present. Actions use authenticated REST requests and bounded job polling. We do not claim Canva webhook signature verification. Confirm there are no subscriptions configured externally; future webhook support must verify Canva signatures and reject replayed or invalid events before processing.

answers.label: Canva data collected and stored
answers.answer: We store encrypted OAuth tokens, expiry/scopes, connection status, Canva user/team and design/asset IDs, source mappings, import versions/pages and operation audit identifiers in Supabase Postgres. Edited image files are stored in Supabase Storage generated-assets under the user's workspace asset path. Temporary export links are processed server-side and are not persisted as asset identity. The integration does not fetch Canva profile email or all library designs.

answers.label: Storage locations and subprocessors
answers.answer: Logical storage is Supabase Postgres and Supabase Storage; the hosting server processes Canva requests and image bytes. Canva receives user-selected images and design content. Actual Supabase/hosting countries, replicas, backup locations and processor contracts have not been verified and require operator confirmation before submission. User-selected publishing or other Mellox workflows may send imported assets to the selected service.

answers.label: Retention periods
answers.answer: There is no implemented fixed calendar retention period for Canva assets, mappings or audit records. OAuth state is valid for ten minutes; that is not a deletion deadline. Finalized states are deleted after installation. Tokens and pending states are removed on disconnect. Imported assets and revoked connection metadata remain with workspace content. Expired abandoned-state cleanup and backup retention rules still need definition and implementation.

answers.label: Disconnect and revocation
answers.answer: An authenticated workspace editor can disconnect Canva in Mellox Connections. A database transaction withdraws pending authorization, marks connection metadata revoked and deletes local tokens. Mellox then attempts Canva token revocation. Non-success or network failures are reported as unconfirmed, with instructions to remove Mellox in Canva account settings. Imported designs/assets remain. Remote revocation retries are not scheduled after local deletion.

answers.label: Data deletion
answers.answer: Disconnect deletes authorization, not imported content. Workspace owners can use the typed-confirmation deletion flow, which now withdraws Canva access before database cascades remove workspace records. Object-storage cleanup is best effort, without guaranteed retry or backup erasure. A user-account erasure and ownership-transfer workflow was not found. Retention, deletion deadlines and backup handling require operator confirmation; we do not guarantee complete erasure.

answers.label: Backups and recovery
answers.answer: Backup configuration, storage countries, encryption, frequency, retention and restore-drill evidence were not verified in this repository audit. We cannot truthfully certify a backup period or recovery guarantee from the source code. The operator must confirm the actual Supabase and hosting settings and establish how deleted Canva data remains excluded after a restore before making affirmative backup or deletion claims.

answers.label: SAST practices
answers.answer: Existing CI includes TypeScript, ESLint and a custom tracked-file secret scan. A dedicated Semgrep 1.180.0 workflow has now been prepared for PRs, main/master pushes and weekly scans using p/security-audit, failing on findings with metrics disabled. The workflow has not yet run or been triaged, so we do not claim an established or clean SAST program. Verify a successful run and branch-protection settings before claiming enforced scanning.

answers.label: SCA and dependency vulnerability handling
answers.answer: CI defines npm audit for production Node dependencies on PRs and main/master pushes, failing at high severity. The local audit on 2026-10-12 found six moderate findings and no high or critical findings. Fixes require compatibility review; they were not automatically applied. This does not establish vulnerability-free dependencies or SCA for development/Python dependencies. Production CI execution and required-check enforcement remain to be verified.
